theorem.statement: For every canonical square size L>=3, the maximum inverse multiplicity of the frozen shortest/left-to-right/lexicographic residual-path map is at least L.

construction.target: j_star equals 1 on every horizontal edge and 0 on every vertical edge, so every horizontal residual edge points right-to-left.
construction.preimages: For each row r, toggle the L-1 horizontal edges of row r in j_star to obtain the distinct state j_r.
construction.selector: In j_r, row r is a left-to-right residual crossing of the minimum possible length L-1. Other rows remain right-to-left crossings of the same length, so the frozen direction tie-break selects row r before every right-to-left candidate.
construction.common_image: T(j_r) toggles row r and returns j_star for every r. Hence j_star has at least L distinct preimages.

theorem.consequence: No L-independent inverse-multiplicity bound exists for the frozen deterministic transport, including at p=1/2 where action weights are flat.

interpretation.closed: The frozen residual-path selector cannot be used as a bounded-to-one midpoint coupling.
interpretation.not_closed: The result does not rule out fractional mass transport, another selector, or vanishing/nonvanishing midpoint LER.
